title: Cut the two straps off a delivered carton with a concealed-blade safety cutter, holding each strap down as it is cut
instruction: Cut both straps on this carton with the safety cutter, holding each strap down while you cut it. Do not mark the carton. Then put the cutter down on the table.
context: Opening delivered cartons is everyday receiving work: stockers and order fillers (O*NET 53-7065.00; 2,804,300 employed in 2025) "Receive, unload, open, unpack, or issue sales floor merchandise." A strapped carton's straps come off first. A safety cutter made for strapping has its blade hidden across a 4 mm channel behind a toe, so the only way to cut is to lay the toe flat on the carton beyond the strap and draw it back under a strap that is tight against the board, until the strap rides up into the channel. A strapping maker's safety booklet gives the rest: "Stand to one side of the strap being cut", "Hold the strap firmly against the package - above the cutter". So one hand bears on the strap beside the cut while the other draws the cutter, without digging its toe into the carton or dragging the carton off its boards. A toe held a millimetre high goes over the strap and cuts nothing.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table. Two pine 1x4 boards (1.9 x 8.9, 30 long) lie flat across the table (long way along y), their middle lines at x 24.5 and 49.5. On them stands a single-wall C-flute kraft corrugated carton, 30.5 x 22.9 x 7.6 (12 x 9 x 3 in), closed and packed to 2.5 kg, its 30.5 side along x, centre at (37.0, 0); its top is 9.5 above the table. Two black polypropylene straps, 1.27 wide (1/2 in) and 0.66 mm thick, run round its 22.9 x 7.6 girth at x 30.5 and x 43.5, passing under it between the boards, each at about 48 N (5 kg) of tension. To the right, two 19 cm offcuts of the same board lie flat with a 1.5 gap between them along x, the gap's middle line at y -26.0, from x 17.5 to 36.5. In the gap stands a concealed-blade safety knife (Martor SECUMAX 320: 15.8 x 1.3 x 5.6, 48 g, blade hidden across a 4 mm channel between its toe and upper jaw) on edge: its toe's tip on the table at (30.0, -26.0) pointing at the robot, its head away from the robot, its handle's end on the table, so it sits nose up by 16 degrees. Both arms start in their rest pose. Layout B (STRAP_LOT=B): carton, boards and straps 1.2 nearer the robot.
scoring: Scored at the end from the video, a ruler and a look at the carton. 0 for the whole trial if a strap was cut while the other gripper was not holding it down (not touching that strap on the carton's top within 12 cm of the cut from 0.1 s before it parted until it parted; the simulator also requires at least 1 N of contact force, so a hover does not count), if the cutter was pressed into the carton (a crease, dent or cut in its top; in the simulator 15 N or more for 0.1 s), or if the carton ends more than 3 cm from its start or tipped more than 10 degrees. Otherwise: 1.0 both straps cut through, the cutter put down on the table (its toe within 3 cm of the table top) and at rest, both grippers at least 3 cm from carton and cutter, the carton at rest; 0.75 both straps cut but one of those missing; 0.5 one strap cut; 0.25 the cutter was lifted 5 cm from where it waits; else 0. Not scored: where along its top a strap is cut, which hand does what, where the cut straps end up.
reset_notes: Each trial uses up two straps: strap the carton again round its girth at the two marks (hand tensioner and buckle, or a strapping machine at its lowest setting, about 5 kg), put it back at its marks on the boards and stand the cutter between its guides. Replace the carton if its top is creased.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz. Each strap: 24 rigid links (1 mm thick, 4 g each; real strap 0.66 mm, about 4 g in all) on ball joints with one sprung slide; 48 N, a strapping machine's lowest setting. Cutting is a rule: a link pressing on the blade with 5 N for 0.1 s parts the strap (estimate). A cut strap does not spring back (links catch on the carton's edges), so the recoil hazard is not simulated; the hold is scored as stated practice. Cutter built from the maker's envelope; carton rigid.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper went to the cutter once and came away without it; no strap was touched); demo: 1.0 on layouts A and B, each at step 612 of 1,500 (demo video: overhead beside the right wrist camera)
